thesis: GAIA is a funded plan for a loop, not yet a forecaster: fast stand-in models redrawn every time new rain, ground-shaking, satellite or groundwater readings arrive, which is the only way to catch the rain, quake, later-storm chain that kills people on Alaska slopes, and it can only sharpen where instruments exist.
supporting_facts: c8 chain: rain soaks, quake weakens, later storm brings it down
c9 surrogate models couple to observations
c14 Wrangell six killed Nov 2023, c12/c13 Haines Dec 2020
counterpoint: Nothing is built, the award record is the only public source, UW holds the larger partner award ($2,209,093), and agents are a planned prototype. A loop updates only where data exists.
falsifiability: False if the record showed pilot results, a model running on a named Alaska slope, or a single-sensor or offline-simulation design.
runner_ups: Skeptic: held to funded-to-try, integration before prediction (merged as the Test act)
Enthusiast: Fairbanks as build end and ASF in the same town (grafted as the Alaska-advantage beat)
guardrails: plan language only: aims, plans, would
never say UAF leads the whole collaboration
no wave height for Barry Arm
